In March this year, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed that it had no intention of launching a new generation of Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg published a new report today, further revealing Apple's Mac Pro strategy and disclosing a surprising inside story—a certain plan that Apple had once developed...

Inside Apple's shelved Mac Pro plans

In the latest issue of his "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman pointed out that discontinuing the Mac Pro "was never Apple's original internal plan." Gurman once again mentioned a previously reported view: Apple's original idea was to launch a chip named "Extreme" on top of the "Ultra" chip.

The report quoted: "It is understood that Apple had developed the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme chips, but ultimately shelved the projects due to cost and demand considerations."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware in development, Gurman said Apple had two models (codenamed J170 and J190) in the pipeline, but neither ultimately saw the light of day.

Perhaps the most intriguing point in the report is that one of the models was equipped with an Intel processor:

Apple eventually discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its official website, and directed buyers to purchase the Mac Studio instead. Although this ending had long been foreshadowed, for Mac Pro hardware enthusiasts, it still marks the quiet end of an era.

What do you think about Apple abandoning the Mac Pro product line rather than continuing the development of the "Extreme" chip in the Apple Silicon era? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
